outcome: Help streaming teams prevent avoidable playback failures and understand retention drivers across devices, networks, content and plans.
overview: Streaming services lose subscribers to problems they can see only in aggregate: slow startup on a particular device, rebuffering on one network at peak, playback errors confined to an older app build. This solution joins player, CDN, network and subscription telemetry into one view of quality of experience, predicts degradation early enough to reroute delivery or adjust bitrate ladders, and explains which cohorts are actually at risk rather than inferring churn from correlation. Delivery cost per streamed hour is tracked alongside quality so neither is improved at the other’s expense. An 8–12 week proof of value targets fewer avoidable playback failures and measurable, holdout-tested retention effects.

benefits.text: Reduce avoidable playback failures and rebuffering on the device and network combinations that cause most complaints
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Validated against the customer’s own QoE baseline during the pilot; last-mile network conditions remain outside the service’s control — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Shorten incident detection and response during live events through predictive QoE alerting
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on telemetry coverage across players and CDNs, and on rehearsed runbooks being followed

benefits.text: Lower delivery cost per streamed hour without degrading measured quality of experience
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on CDN contract structure and encoding-ladder headroom; every cost change is gated on QoE not regressing

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); playback telemetry, subscription events and support records remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, with viewer-level data minimised and aggregated wherever the analysis allows

notFor.situation: Player and CDN telemetry is not instrumented or is not comparable across platforms
notFor.why: Every conclusion depends on consistent session-level QoE measurement; partial telemetry produces confident conclusions about the wrong cohorts

notFor.situation: Automated delivery changes without human approval are expected
notFor.why: Automated rerouting and ladder changes can amplify an incident across an entire audience; the design requires canaries, approvals and a rehearsed rollback

notFor.situation: Churn causation is expected from observational data alone
notFor.why: QoE and churn correlate strongly, but attributing cancellations to quality without a holdout confuses content, pricing and seasonal effects with delivery

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns delivery configuration, on-call operations and every production change decision · Duration: 8–12 week PoV; further 16–28 weeks to full production operations
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, streaming engineer, data engineer, ML engineer; customer streaming-engineering owner, site reliability lead, product manager, privacy reviewer · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option, with event-day enhanced cover; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and QoE baseline agreement
2) Telemetry integration and session-store build
3) Alerting, prediction and service-level-objective configuration
4) Load, failure and canary rollback testing including a live-event rehearsal
5) Controlled rollout with runbooks and operations UAT
6) Stabilisation and handover
deliverables: Telemetry and QoE metrics reconcile with player and CDN sources within the agreed tolerance
Load and failure tests pass at the agreed peak concurrency
Canary rollout and rollback demonstrated on a production-like cohort
DRM and territorial rights boundaries respected by every delivery action
Experiment design agreed with product and operations UAT complete
effort: 8–12 week PoV; further 16–28 weeks to full production operations
